title: Halcyon Systems - POC capacity & autoscale scoping
summary: POC scoping focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling strategy. Customer runs mixed realtime and batch LLM workloads (chat + semantic search) with spikes during business hours. Discussed reserved GPUs for baseline throughput, burst on demand for peak traffic, KV/prefix caching, fallback to smaller quantized models, success criteria (latency P50/P95, throughput, cost targets), benchmarks to run during POC, and a 4-week timeline with rollup milestones.
action_items: Alex Carter - send POC proposal & pricing ranges (reserved + burst) by 2026-12-07
Priya Singh - share benchmark spreadsheet and sample load scripts by 2026-12-06
Sofia Martinez - provide 3 representative prompt sets and token length distribution by 2026-12-08
Daniel Cho - confirm VPC peering & egress constraints and provide network diagram by 2026-12-09
next_steps: Redwood to provision 2x reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline POC (estimated)
Customer to run initial synthetic benchmark using Redwood-provided load scripts next week
Schedule technical deep dive with infra + security to discuss VPC/on-prem options (w/ security docs)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Carter (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got Jamal, Sofia, Daniel and Maya from Halcyon, and Priya and Marco from our side. Quick intro and we'll jump into capacity.
[00:18] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): Hey thanks Alex, we've been running prototypes in house but want a POC to validate cost and SLA improvements, mainly latency at scale and predictable billing.
[00:34] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Great; can you give us a bit of context on the workload? Mix of chat, embeddings, any batch re-rank?
[00:45] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): Yeah it's about 60% chat-ish user interactions, 30% embeddings for semantic search, and 10% heavier rerank jobs. Typical prompt lengths are 60-300 tokens, avg around 140. We do peak traffic 10am-2pm PST where qps jumps 4-5x.
[01:10] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): Also need to call out DR requirements, our corp policy wants fallback if GPUs are saturated, and we can't have more than 30s cold-starts for customer-facing queries.
[01:25] Marco Li (Redwood): Okay noted. For POC we'll look at reserved GPUs for baseline throughput and a burst pool for peaks, plus fallback policies to smaller quantized variants.
[01:36] Alex Carter (Redwood): Goal is to size reserved capacity to cover 95th percentile during normal hours, and let burst handle spikes. What are your cost targets?
[01:46] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): We'd like cost per 1k tokens to be competitive with our current self-host numbers - roughly $0.40/1k tokens as a target, but more important is keeping P95 latency under 800ms for chat.
[02:02] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Okay P95 800ms is reasonable with proper batching and KV cache for short prefixes. For the reservation, based on your numbers and avg 140 tokens, my quick calc is ~2 reserved A100-equivalents to hit baseline ~60 rps sustained? We'll validate.
[02:24] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): That seems light. Our internal tests show 80 rps at 150 tokens per second with a 4 GPU cluster. There might be inefficiencies in our stack.
[02:36] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Totally - POC benchmark will reconcile. We'll run two benchmark profiles: synthetic steady-state and production-realistic (spiky with session affinity).
[02:48] Maya Patel (Halcyon): Timeline expectation? We have exec buy-in but need results in ~4 weeks to decide vendor.
[02:56] Alex Carter (Redwood): 4 weeks is doable. Week 0-1: infra hookup and dataset/prompts, Week 2: reserved baseline benchmarks, Week 3: burst/fallback testing, Week 4: report and cost modeling.
[03:10] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): Security/regulatory: SOC2 + audit logs + KMS is mandatory. Can you provide details?
[03:18] Marco Li (Redwood): Yes we'll share SOC2 report and docs; for POC we can enable customer-managed KMS in Private mode if needed, otherwise we provide audit exported logs.
[03:27] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): Network: we prefer VPC peering to avoid NAT egress costs and ensure low latency. Is that supported?
[03:33] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Yes VPC peering is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we have secure VPN options. We'll include network diagram in the doc pack.
[03:44] Alex Carter (Redwood): Back to capacity: for burst strategy we typically recommend a small reserved pool sized to baseline + a burst pool using pre-warmed instances to avoid cold-starts. We can also configure a fallback policy: when both reserved and burst are saturated, route to a smaller quantized model or increase response trimming.
[04:05] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): What about autoscaling latency? If burst uses cold-started GPUs that adds 10s-30s which is too slow for customer queries.
[04:15] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Right - we avoid cold starts by pre-warming a minimal set of instances based on time-of-day scheduling and predicted spikes. For unpredictable spikes we suggest an elastic buffer with queued requests and graceful degradation - e.g., return cached responses or fall back to 1.5B quantized model for most queries.
[04:34] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): We need concrete SLAs during POC: P50/P95 latency numbers, throughput targets, and cost per token.
[04:42] Alex Carter (Redwood): We'll document targets: P50 < 200ms, P95 < 800ms for chat flows; embeddings P95 < 1.5s; throughput baseline 60-80 rps for chat; cost target per your target. We'll add these to success criteria.
[05:02] Marco Li (Redwood): For benchmarking plan: we'll run three phases: 1) unit perf (single request latency distribution), 2) cluster scale (sustained qps with reserved capacity), 3) spike/burst (simulate 5x traffic for 10-20 min). We'll measure cpu/gpu utilization, token/sec, KV hit rate, per-request latency percentiles, and costs.
[05:28] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): Can you run our rerank jobs? They are long - up to 2k tokens sometimes.
[05:35] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Yes rerank will go into batch queue testing. We'll provision separate job queues so they don't starve chat traffic; and we can isolate on dedicated GPUs if needed.
[05:48] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): Any thought on model quantization and quality tradeoffs? Our product team is very sensitive to hallucinations.
[05:57] Marco Li (Redwood): We'll include quality checks: sampling outputs from quantized variants vs baseline full-precision model on your eval set. If degradation > threshold we won't use the quantized path for customer-facing queries.
[06:10] Maya Patel (Halcyon): Who owns the bootstrapping of prompts and eval sets?
[06:15] Alex Carter (Redwood): Halcyon to provide prompt sets (Sofia) and we'll seed the eval harness; Priya will run the quality comparisons and provide a report.
[06:25] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): On fallback policies: prefer degrade quality gracefully rather than full failure. For example, reduce context window or shorten outputs before moving to smaller model.
[06:36] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): Agreed - policy options: 1) reduce context / trim tokens, 2) send to quantized 2B model, 3) return cached previous response with a flag; we can tune thresholds.
[06:50] Alex Carter (Redwood): For cost visibility we'll enable token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console during POC. That'll help you map cost to product features.
[07:00] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): Nice. For the reserved GPU spec, you mentioned A100-equivalent - any chance we can get vCPU/memory numbers for sizing?
[07:09] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): We'll include instance types in the doc. Roughly 80-100GB GPU RAM equivalents for full LLM models, and host nodes with 64-128 vCPU for pre/post-processing. We'll confirm exact SKUs in proposal.
[07:24] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): Benchmarks: want reproducible scripts.
[07:28] Marco Li (Redwood): We'll share a bench repo and load scripts; you'll run them in your environment and also against Redwood hosted endpoints for apples-to-apples.
[07:36] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): Regarding burst billing, how do you charge for reserved vs burst vs pre-warm capacity?
[07:42] Alex Carter (Redwood): Reserved is monthly commit; burst billed hourly on consumption and pre-warmed instances billed at a lower hourly rate when idle. We'll include pricing ranges in proposal.
[07:54] Maya Patel (Halcyon): Ok timeline recap?
[07:58] Alex Carter (Redwood): Week 1: connect infra and share docs (SOC2, network diagram), Week 2: baseline reserved benchmarks, Week 3: burst/fallback testing and quality evals, Week 4: final report and cost model. Decision milestone end of Week 4.
[08:14] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
[08:18] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): Need to confirm IAM roles and approve peering; should be quick but I'll get it scheduled.
[08:24] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): One more thing: for autoscaling policies we suggest hybrid triggers - CPU/GPU utilization + queue length + request latency. That avoids scaling solely on util which can be noisy.
[08:39] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): Good point. Also want to set circuit-breaker thresholds so we can failover to read-only cached responses when latency > 2s.
[08:48] Marco Li (Redwood): We'll prototype circuit-breaker rules and include them in the POC runbook.
[08:55] Alex Carter (Redwood): Let's capture action items - we'll follow up with proposal and bench scripts. Any final Qs?
[09:02] Maya Patel (Halcyon): Can we get a short exec summary to share?
[09:06] Alex Carter (Redwood): Yes we'll send an exec one-pager with cost ballpark and timeline.
[09:12] Jamal Reyes (Halcyon): Thanks everyone.
[09:15] Sofia Martinez (Halcyon): Thanks.
[09:18] [call continues with clarifying questions about prompt examples and then moves to share links]
[12:45] Priya Singh (Redwood SE): (shares link) https://redwood.example.com/poc-benchmarks - bench repo and sheet.
[13:12] Daniel Cho (Halcyon): We'll try the bench scripts Thursday and report numbers.
[13:25] Alex Carter (Redwood): Great. Recap: Redwood to provision tentative reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent), provide bench scripts and SOC2, Halcyon to provide prompts and network info. Follow ups next Tue for mid-POC sync.
[13:45] End of call
notes: Transcript contains typical speech disfluencies and occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., model names and instance SKUs). Links shared are placeholders.
meeting_length_notes: discussion roughly 40-42 minutes; timestamps in transcript are rough markers, not exact second-level alignment
